'''Gilbert Ronald Bainbridge''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FInstP}} (28 November 1925 – 13 August 2003) was a British physicist and engineer. After working for the [[United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority]], he became professor of energy studies and director of the Energy Centre at [[Newcastle University]].

==Early life and education==
Gilbert Ronald Bainbridge was born on 28 November 1925 in [[Felling, Tyne and Wear|Felling]], [[County Durham]]. He attended Jarrow County Secondary School before studying physics at [[Durham University]], graduating with honours in 1946.<ref>{{cite book |title=Graduates of the University |date=1960 |publisher=University of Durham |page=30 |url=https://reed.dur.ac.uk/xtf/view?docId=bookreader/DU_Calendars/DurhamGraduates/DurhamGraduatesMETSfile.xml#page/28/mode/2up |access-date=18 August 2026}}</ref>

He remained at Durham for doctoral research under [[Arthur Prowse|W. A. Prowse]], receiving his PhD in 1953 for a thesis entitled ''The Emission of Ionizing Radiation during a Spark Discharge''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Bainbridge |first=Gilbert Ronald |title=The Emission of Ionizing Radiation during a Spark Discharge |degree=PhD |publisher=Durham University |year=1953 |url=http://etheses.dur.ac.uk/9231/ |access-date=7 February 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Bainbridge began his academic career as a lecturer at [[University of the West of Scotland|Paisley Technical College]] in 1951. In 1954, he moved to [[McMaster University]] in [[Hamilton, Ontario]], Canada, where his research included the measurement of atomic masses using mass spectrometry.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Eastman |first1=Philip C. |last2=Isenor |first2=Neil R. |last3=Bainbridge |first3=G. R. |last4=Duckworth |first4=Henry E. |date=1 January 1956 |title=Atomic Masses of Ni58 and Ni60 |journal=Physical Review |volume=103 |issue=1 |pages=145–146 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.103.145 |quote=Department of Physics, Hamilton College, McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario |bibcode=1956PhRv..103..145E}}</ref>

In 1957, Bainbridge joined the [[United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority]] (UKAEA) at [[Warrington]] as an assistant chief engineer.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Willding-Jones |first1=James |last2=Oswick |first2=Chris |date=19 March 1971 |title=Playtime on a nuclear Karken |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/daily-post-merseyside-ed-playtime-on/145731305/ |work=Daily Post |page=6 |access-date=20 April 2024}}</ref> He subsequently worked on the development of nuclear reactors and associated research facilities. By 1974, he was manager of technical assessments in the UKAEA's Reactor Group.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Bainbridge |first=G. R. |title=Nuclear Options |journal=Nature |volume=249 |issue=5459 |year=1974 |pages=733–737 |doi=10.1038/249733a0}}</ref>

In August 1974, Bainbridge left the UKAEA to take up the newly established chair of energy studies at [[Newcastle University]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Bainbridge |first=G. R. |title=Energy in the OECD |journal=Nature |volume=254 |issue=5502 |date=24 April 1975 |pages=644–645 |doi=10.1038/254644a0}}</ref>
